Diabetes.summary: Low glycemic index, controlled carbohydrates, high fiber (ADA 2024)
Diabetes.meal_timing: Eat at consistent times; avoid skipping meals

Hypertension.summary: Low sodium DASH diet, high potassium and magnesium (ACC/AHA 2017)
Hypertension.meal_timing: Reduce portion size; spread meals evenly

Heart Disease.meal_timing: Small frequent meals; avoid large meals

Obesity.summary: Calorie-controlled, high fiber, low sugar (WHO guidelines)
Obesity.meal_timing: Structured meal times; no late-night eating; mindful eating

Celiac Disease.summary: Strict gluten-free diet (no wheat, barley, rye)
Celiac Disease.meal_timing: No special timing; focus on strict gluten avoidance

Lactose Intolerance.summary: Limit or avoid dairy products; use lactase enzyme
Lactose Intolerance.meal_timing: Start with small amounts of dairy to test tolerance
Lactose Intolerance.authority: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

Kidney Disease.summary: Low potassium, low phosphorus, low protein, low sodium (KDIGO 2022)
Kidney Disease.meal_timing: Regular meal pattern; consult dietitian for fluid restrictions

High Cholesterol.summary: Low saturated fat, high soluble fiber, sterols/stanols (NCEP ATP III)
High Cholesterol.meal_timing: Consistent eating pattern; avoid skipping meals
High Cholesterol.authority: NCEP ATP III, AHA 2019 Cholesterol Guidelines

PCOS.summary: Low GI, anti-inflammatory, high fiber (Endocrine Society)
PCOS.meal_timing: Small frequent meals to maintain blood sugar levels

Thyroid Disorder.summary: Moderate iodine, limit raw goitrogens, adequate selenium
eat_less: Raw cruciferous vegetables in large amounts
Thyroid Disorder.meal_timing: Take thyroid medication 30-60 min before eating

Anemia.summary: Iron-rich foods with Vitamin C for absorption (WHO/NIH)
eat_less: Tea and coffee with meals (blocks iron absorption)
Anemia.meal_timing: Pair iron-rich foods with Vitamin C at each meal
Anemia.authority: WHO Iron Deficiency Guidelines, NIH Office of Dietary Supplements

Gout.summary: Low purine diet, stay hydrated, avoid fructose (ACR 2020)
Gout.meal_timing: Stay hydrated (8+ glasses water/day); avoid alcohol

IBS.summary: Low FODMAP diet, moderate fiber, avoid triggers (NICE/Monash)
avoid_completely: High-FODMAP trigger foods specific to individual
IBS.meal_timing: Regular meal times; avoid large meals; sit down to eat
IBS.authority: Monash University Low FODMAP, NICE CG61

Liver Disease.summary: Low fat, low sodium, adequate protein but not excess (EASL 2018)
Liver Disease.meal_timing: Small frequent meals; late evening snack if needed
Liver Disease.authority: European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) 2018

GERD.summary: Low fat, low sugar, avoid acidic and trigger foods (NIDDK/ACG)
GERD.meal_timing: Eat 3 hours before lying down; small frequent meals

Osteoporosis.summary: High calcium, adequate Vitamin D, low sodium (National Osteoporosis Foundation)
Osteoporosis.meal_timing: Spread calcium intake throughout the day for better absorption

Rheumatoid Arthritis.summary: Anti-inflammatory Mediterranean diet, low saturated fat (Arthritis Foundation)
Rheumatoid Arthritis.meal_timing: Regular anti-inflammatory meals; maintain healthy weight

NAFLD.summary: Low fructose, low fat, reduced calorie (AASLD/EASL)
NAFLD.authority: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)

Gallbladder Disease.summary: Very low fat -- fat triggers gallbladder contraction (ACG)
Gallbladder Disease.meal_timing: Small low-fat meals throughout the day; avoid large meals

Crohn's Disease.summary: Low fiber during flares, low FODMAP, low fat (CCFA/Crohn's Foundation)
Crohn's Disease.meal_timing: Small frequent meals; keep food diary to identify triggers

Chronic Pancreatitis.summary: Extremely low fat -- most critical nutritional restriction (APA/EPC)
Chronic Pancreatitis.meal_timing: 6 small meals per day; pancreatic enzyme supplements with meals
Chronic Pancreatitis.authority: American Pancreatic Association (APA), European Pancreatic Club

Migraine.summary: Avoid tyramine, MSG, and dietary triggers (American Migraine Foundation)
Migraine.meal_timing: Never skip meals; maintain consistent eating schedule; stay hydrated
